title: How to enroll in the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge
summary: You don't sign up for the Bridge yourself. Your doctor submits a prior authorization, and one easy-to-miss step has to happen first.
body_text: How to enroll in the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge Brandon Ballinger · Jul 1, 2026 Medicare covers GLP-1s for $50/month starting July 1, but patients don’t sign up directly. Instead their doctor needs to fax in a prior authorization form for the bridge . This post describes what patients should know about eligibility for the Medicare’s GLP-1 Bridge program. It covers how the Bridge actually gets turned on, whether you’re likely to qualify, what to bring to your doctor to speed things up, and what happens at the pharmacy. For the full policy background (why the Bridge exists, how long it lasts, how it fits with Medicare’s other GLP-1 coverage), see Medicare covers GLP-1s for $50/month . You check eligibility and talk to your doctor. Your doctor handles the prior authorization. The pharmacy charges a fixed $50 monthly copay. How do you sign up for the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge? You don’t sign up directly, and that’s by design. Submission is restricted to prescribing clinicians, so the work happens in your doctor’s office. The sequence looks like this: Your pharmacy runs a claim that gets denied. Bridge drugs route through a dedicated billing channel. The first claim is expected to come back denied, which is what tells the system a Bridge prior authorization is needed. This is a normal step, not a rejection of your coverage. Your doctor submits the prior authorization. They complete the CMS GLP-1 Bridge form and send it electronically (through CoverMyMeds) or by fax. The form asks for your BMI at the time you started a GLP-1 and which qualifying conditions you have. You fill the prescription for $50. Once approved, you pay a fixed $50 copay per monthly supply. So your job is really steps you do with your doctor: confirm you’re eligible, and give them the information they need to fill out the form correctly the first time. Are you eligible for the GLP-1 Bridge? The Bridge covers GLP-1s prescribed for weight loss when you’re 18 or older and meet a BMI threshold paired with the right condition: Your BMI What else you need 35 or higher Nothing else required 30 or higher Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, uncontrolled high blood pressure, or chronic kidney disease (stage 3a or higher) 27 or higher Pre-diabetes, a prior heart attack, a prior stroke, or symptomatic peripheral artery disease BMI is measured at the point you started a GLP-1, not where you are today. If you began semaglutide two years ago at a BMI of 37 and you’re now at 32, you still qualify. The full eligibility rules, including how the Bridge interacts with Medicare’s existing coverage for diabetes and cardiovascular disease, are in the main coverage post . What to bring to your doctor The prior authorization goes faster when your doctor has the answers the form wants. Before your visit, gather: Your starting BMI. The weight and height from when you first began a GLP-1, if you’ve been on one. If you’re starting fresh, your current numbers. Your qualifying conditions. Pre-diabetes, prior heart attack or stroke, peripheral artery disease, heart failure, kidney disease, or blood pressure readings on your current medications. Your current medications , especially blood pressure drugs, since uncontrolled hypertension is defined as readings above 140/90 despite two of them. Several of these conditions are confirmed by lab work rather than symptoms. Pre-diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and the markers behind cardiovascular risk often show up on a blood panel before you’d notice anything. What does the GLP-1 Bridge cost? You pay $50 per monthly supply, and that amount doesn’t change based on where you are in your Part D benefit. It’s worth knowing that the $50 does not count toward your Part D out-of-pocket cap, and manufacturer coupons can’t be applied to Bridge claims. For comparison, cash prices for these drugs usually run $1,000 to $1,400 a month. The cost details are covered in full in the coverage post . Why was my pharmacy claim denied first? Because the system is built that way. The denied claim is the trigger that tells Medicare a Bridge prior authorization should be created. If your pharmacist tells you the first claim came back denied, that’s the process working, not a sign you’ve been turned down. Your doctor’s prior authorization is the next step, and it’s what actually opens coverage. If you want the clinical detail (which 12 questions are on the form, how your provider submits it, and what holds up an approval), we wrote a companion piece for clinicians: the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge prior authorization form, explained . This post is part of our series on Medicare coverage for cardiovascular health . See also: Medicare covers GLP-1s for $50/month and the GLP-1 Bridge prior authorization form . Several Bridge-qualifying conditions are confirmed by lab work, not symptoms. Empirical Health's heart health panel measures the markers behind pre-diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and cardiovascular risk, so you and your doctor have the data to fill out the prior authorization with confidence. title: 生成AIを活用した小学生向け「遠隔AIクリエイター教室」をKDDIとエリクソンで初開催
summary: KDDIとエリクソン・ジャパンは、仙台市教育委員会の後援のもと、2026年9月5日（土）・6日（日）の2日間、小学3年生から6年生までを対象に、生成AIをテーマにした「遠隔AIクリエイター教室」（以下、本イベント）を開催します。それに伴い、2026年7月31日（金）から、各回15名の参加募集を開始します。
body_text: KDDI株式会社（本社：東京都港区、代表取締役社長 CEO：松田 浩路、以下 KDDI）とエリクソン・ジャパン株式会社（本社：東京都港区、代表取締役社長：安東 宏昭、ジャワッド・マンスール、以下 エリクソン・ジャパン）は、仙台市教育委員会の後援のもと、2026年9月5日（土）・6日（日）の2日間、小学3年生から6年生までを対象に、生成AIをテーマにした「遠隔AIクリエイター教室」（以下、本イベント）を開催します。それに伴い、2026年7月31日（金）から、各回15名の参加募集を開始します。 KDDIとエリクソン・ジャパンはこれまで、ロボットやゲーム、ドローンでのプログラミングを題材にした遠隔STEAM教室を開催し、遠く離れた場所の子どもたちがまるでひとつの空間にいるかのように繋がり、ICTスキルを共に学べる環境を提供することで、全国の教育機会格差の解消に取り組んできました。 本イベントは、未来を担う子どもたちの思いを実現し、夢や希望を届け、可能性を広げる機会を提供したいという思いから、パートナーとの共創により発足した活動「KDDIみらい共創プログラム」の一環として実施します。なお、生成AIをテーマにした遠隔STEAM教室はKDDI初の取り組みです。 ■ プログラムの特長：生成 AIとの対話で育む「未来を創造する力」 本イベントでは、Google のAI「Gemini」を活用し、東京と仙台の参加者が合同チームを組んで学ぶ、実践型のAI学習プログラムを提供します。 東京・仙台の子どもたちが、遠隔で協働して学ぶ 東京と仙台の参加者が合同チームを組み、離れた場所にいながら一緒に課題に取り組みます。地域を越えて意見を交わしながら学び、多様な仲間と協力する体験を通じて、コミュニケーション力を育みます。 生成AIと対話しながら、「理想の未来」を描く 参加者は、社会課題について生成AIと対話を重ねながら、「どうすれば社会がもっと良くなるか」という未来の姿を考えます。さらに、チームで導き出した「良くなる未来の姿」を生成AIでビジュアル化し、自分たちのアイデアが形になる達成感を味わいます。 AIの便利さだけでなく、正しい付き合い方も学ぶ 生成AIの利便性だけでなく、情報の正確性や倫理的課題といった「AIとの正しい付き合い方やリスク」についても座学を通じて学びます。最先端技術を「パートナー」として活用しながら、論理的思考力や創造力を育みます。 また、本イベントでは、9月21日（月）の「敬老の日」にちなんだカリキュラムも予定しており、親子・祖父母世代を含め、三世代で楽しんでいただける内容です。 ■開催概要 本イベントには、KDDIが全国の「au Style」にて展開中の生成AI教室で培った知見を活用しており、初心者のお子さまでも安心してステップアップできる構成となっており、最先端技術への関心を楽しみながら育むことが可能です。 名称 遠隔AIクリエイター教室 日時 2026年9月5日(土)〜9月6日(日) 1部：13:00-15:00 2部：16:00-18:00 場所 ① KDDI株式会社本社 東京都港区高輪２丁目２１−１ THE LINKPILLAR 1 NORTH ② au Style SENDAI 宮城県仙台市青葉区一番町3-8-8 参加対象 小学3年生～小学6年生、各回15名（2日間計：120名） ・1部（東京/仙台）：各15名 ・2部（東京/仙台）：各15名 ※保護者の方のご同伴をお願いいたします。 ※参加者数は変更となる場合があります。 参加費 無料 実施内容 title: Bridger Aerospace Secures DOI Task Order, Deploying Its Most Advanced Multi-Mission Wildfire Aircraft
summary: King Air 350 configured with aircraft modification updates, dual-sensor configuration, and ability to pair with interoperable intel BELGRADE,…...
body_text: Bridger Aerospace Secures DOI Task Order, Deploying Its Most Advanced Multi-Mission Wildfire Aircraft July 16, 2026 8:30am EDT Download as PDF King Air 350 configured with aircraft modification updates, dual-sensor configuration, and ability to pair with interoperable intel BELGRADE, Mont., July 16, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Bridger Aerospace Group Holdings, Inc. (“Bridger,” “Bridger Aerospace” or the “Company”) (NASDAQ: BAER, BAERW), one of the nation’s leading aerial firefighting companies, today announced it has been awarded a task order by the U.S. Department of the Interior (DOI) to deploy a King Air 350 equipped with Bridger’s most advanced Multi-Mission Aircraft (MMA) capabilities. Following months of extensive modifications completed at Bridger's FAA-certified repair station, supported by the engineering expertise of the company's Huntsville team, the aircraft has been deployed under a 112-day task order to provide advanced situational awareness in support of wildfire and other emergency operations across the United States. The aircraft is equipped with Blackhawk engine upgrades to deliver jet-like speed, superior loiter time, and outstanding low-altitude performance. This King Air is also enhanced with Garmin avionics, dual sensor systems, and real-time data dissemination capabilities. Its sensor suite includes the first-ever use of Wide Area Motion Imagery (WAMI) technology in wildfire, paired with the proven performance of the MX-15 electro-optical/infrared (EO/IR) sensor. “Our King Air MMA represents Bridger's commitment to combining advanced technology with specialized aircraft to deliver the most innovative wildfire and other emergency intelligence solutions available,” said Bridger CEO Sam Davis. “This project was an extraordinary undertaking for our team, and we believe it has the potential to significantly enhance how intelligence is collected, shared, and acted upon in the field. As we advance our mission to protect lives, property, and the environment, we remain focused on delivering highly capable aircraft, exceptional platform performance, and meaningful value to our partners.” This deployment marks another milestone in Bridger's mission to equip frontline wildfire personnel with the most capable and fully integrated aerial intelligence tools available. The aircraft will operate through the end of October and will be based in Bozeman, Montana, supporting primarily wildfire response efforts as temperatures rise and drought conditions intensify across the western United States. About Bridger Aerospace Based in Belgrade, Montana, Bridger Aerospace Group Holdings, Inc. is one of the nation’s largest aerial firefighting companies. Bridger provides aerial firefighting and wildfire management services to federal and state government agencies, including the United States Forest Service, across the nation, as well as internationally. More information about Bridger Aerospace is available at https://www.bridgeraerospace.com. title: The Refill Revenue You're Leaving on the Table: How Pharmacy Workflow Automation Brings Patients Back
summary: See how independent pharmacies are using pharmacy workflow automation to stop losing refills, reduce prescription abandonment, and grow revenue without adding staff.
body_text: Pharmacy workflow automation has changed what's possible for independent pharmacies managing refills, but refill opportunities might still be slipping through the cracks. ‍ Knowing a patient has an upcoming refill is only half the battle. If the outreach is manual, inconsistent, or easy for patients to ignore, the prescription still doesn't get filled consistently. ‍ The result is the same: poorer medication adherence for patients and lost revenue for the pharmacy. ‍ Where patients fall through the gaps in care ‍ Prescription abandonment doesn't always happen at the point of sale. A lot of it happens quietly, between fills, when a patient's routine slips and nobody follows up. The phone tag cycle is friction that costs everyone – the patient forgets, waits until they're nearly out, calls when your team is slammed, gets put on hold, and maybe calls back late, or simply gives up. ‍ Your staff shouldn't have to manage this process manually, and with the right pharmacy patient communication solution in place, they won't have to. Nimble's refill solution was built to close that gap automatically by helping pharmacies capture more refill revenue, improve patient adherence, and reduce manual follow-up work for staff. ‍ Patients love how Nimble makes refills simple ‍ From our Apple App Store reviews, patients consistently highlight how simple and convenient Nimble makes managing refills. ‍ "I have had a fantastic experience getting my prescription refills. I get a monthly reminder, and it only takes a few clicks to submit the order. They deliver it right to my door. They answer all my questions quickly. It is a wonderful service." ‍ For patients juggling busy schedules, those features go even further. ‍ "I love being able to get notifications about my prescription refills and being able to pay for them before I even get to the pharmacy and easily pick up. It makes life so much simpler especially when my life gets super busy." ‍ How Nimble works to improve refills ‍ Nimble keeps your refill queue full without disrupting how your team already works. Patients stay in control of their refills, and the process is built to reduce your staff’s manual workload. ‍ Step One: The reminder ‍ A few days before a patient runs out of medication based on their prescription, Nimble sends an automated reminder. Once the patient confirms, the refill request is automatically sent to your pharmacy team with no manual follow-up required. ‍ Step Two: Real-time updates ‍ Throughout the process, patients receive real-time status updates so they know exactly when their prescription is ready, ensuring they only show up when it's available for pickup. Your team can view the same estimated timing shown to the patient. ‍ The result is fewer inbound calls, better transparency for patients and staff, and a refill workflow that runs alongside your existing PMS setup without changing it. ‍ Retail pharmacies that activate refills see a 5.4% increase in refills by month two. For specialty pharmacies, that jumps to 17.5%. ‍ Your pharmacy is always in control ‍ Nimble's refill reminders are designed to keep patients engaged without overwhelming them. Pharmacies control which prescriptions are eligible for refills and when reminders are sent, ensuring outreach aligns with their workflow and patient needs. And with patients already using Nimble to manage their prescriptions, refill reminders feel like a seamless part of the experience rather than another communication channel to keep track of. ‍ Nimble’s messaging cadence has been refined over five years of feedback from independent pharmacy partners. It's intentional and designed to stay helpful without becoming noise. ‍ Refill adherence is a direct revenue lever. Every lapsed prescription is a lost fill, and multiplied across your active patient panel, those missed opportunities add up quickly. Nimble gives pharmacies a reliable way to recapture that volume without adding headcount or increasing staff workload. ‍ But the impact goes beyond revenue. When patients refill medications on time, they're more likely to stay adherent to their prescribed therapies, which can lead to better health outcomes and continuity of care. By proactively reminding patients before prescriptions lapse, Nimble helps pharmacies play a more active role in supporting adherence while reducing the risk of gaps in treatment. ‍ "Nimble has also helped our business grow by providing 24/7 online capabilities. Since our patients often work the same hours we are open, they appreciate being able to request refills or use the chat outside of our standard 9-to-6 pharmacy hours. It significantly reduces our staff's workload by cutting down on phone calls and allowing patients to manage their prescriptions on their own time," said Obi Van-Lare, Pharmacist in Charge, Paragon Pharmacy. ‍ This level of automation also frees your team from reactive follow-up tasks, allowing staff to spend more time on high-value activities like medication therapy management (MTM), patient consultations, and other clinical services. The result is a solution that supports both business growth and better patient care. ‍ Save Time and Earn More Revenue with Refills from Nimble ‍ Nimble automates patient outreach and keeps your team informed about refill requests, so nothing slips through the cracks. Patients set their contact preference and receive updates about when their prescription is ready. The feature integrates with your patients’ Nimble experience, so it feels seamless rather than tacked on. Beyond recaptured fills, pharmacy workflow automation at this level supports medication adherence, reduced prescription abandonment, and incremental revenue across the platform. ‍ Ready to Get Started? ‍ Talk to our team to see Nimble in action. ‍

title: Social media management for startups: A complete guide
summary: Learn how startups can manage social media without a full-time team or big budget. Practical steps and a plan that scales as you grow.
body_text: Table of Contents Share Email Share Resource Managing a startup business requires you to spend most of your time and resources on fine-tuning strategy and hands-on operations. So there’s hardly any time left to create content and maintain a social media presence. But with its massive reach and free marketing tools, social media is an indispensable tool for startups. It’s how you get your business in front of the right people and engage them without the heavy ad spend. Fortunately, automation tools help make social media management much more feasible even for busy startup founders. Combined with a strategic approach to platform selection and content production, social media can be the ultimate channel for building a brand presence and attracting customers. This post provides a practical guide on social media management for startups. Let’s take a look. What is social media management for startups? Social media management for startups refers to the strategic process of creating and publishing content on social media to promote a startup business. In addition to content creation and publishing, it encompasses other steps that support your social media marketing strategy , such as analytics and community engagement. For new businesses, managing social media requires actively building brand awareness from scratch. Your goal is to establish trust with an audience that’s never heard of your business before and turn them into actual buyers—all with a limited budget. So unlike established brands that can afford to post erratically or leave their comments unanswered, startups need to be more consistent and responsive. Why social media matters when you’re an early-stage business When you’re just starting out, people don’t really know your brand yet. To gain customers, you need to get your business in front of more people and win their trust. Social media opens the doors to help you do just that, offering a low-cost channel to build awareness and trust. Low-cost trust building before you have brand recognition An active social media presence signals to audiences that your brand is credible, enabling you to build trust over the long run. Source: Instagram Common social media mistakes startups make New businesses find social media overwhelming because they’re trying to do too much without having an actual strategy in place. Here are some of the big mistakes you should avoid when managing social media for your startup. Trying to be everywhere on every platform Having an account on every social media platform seems like the obvious choice when you want to get your business in front of as many people as possible. But this is the easiest way to get overwhelmed as you struggle to push out the occasional post while keeping up with your messages. Sure, you can use cross-posting tools, but that won’t make up for the slow responses and the missed messages when you’re trying to juggle too many platforms. Posting without a strategy or a content calendar Established brands can get away with an erratic posting schedule because they already have a solid presence. Emerging businesses can’t afford to skip this social media best practice . At this stage, you need consistency to stay top of mind and maintain visibility on social media. Too many startups try to tackle social media without a proper content strategy in place. So it keeps them from maintaining a regular publishing schedule. And you can’t win the algorithm or engage audiences when you’re only posting once every few days whenever you have a content idea. Not measuring results Many startups simply push out content hoping for the best. They’re not tracking content performance or measuring results, either because they don’t have the time, or they don’t know how. So there’s no way to know what content resonates with their audience or what formats get the most visibility. Not using a social media management tool Being new to social media management and working with minuscule budgets will have startups doing everything manually. Instead of investing in social media management tools , they’re relying on native publishing features and scheduling each post individually. The biggest con is that these manual tasks take up a significant portion of your time. Plus, you can’t visualize what your content cadence looks like, which makes it difficult to see whether you’re posting too much or not enough. How to build a social media strategy for your startup Startups and smaller operations need to be highly strategic with how they spend their time and resources. A solid social media strategy will help you optimize the management workflow. Here are the essential steps to build a strategy for managing social media for your startup. Set goals tied to business outcomes For startups, every resource spent toward social media marketing should have tangible business outcomes. Whether that’s generating leads or driving brand awareness, your social media goals should directly add value to your business. These goals will then shape the rest of your social media management efforts. Some examples include: Driving leads and revenue: Use social commerce tools and promo offers to generate sales. Building brand awareness: Use paid ads, influencer marketing and user-generated content to get in front of a larger audience. Providing direct customer service: Answer questions promptly and resolve customer complaints through DMs. Collecting market insights: Gather valuable data on content performance, customer behavior and feedback to refine your strategy. Building a brand community: Encourage community conversations and UGC to foster a loyal fanbase. Choose platforms where your audience actually is Smart social media management for startups is all about knowing where to focus your efforts. Pick out a couple of platforms that make the most sense for your business based on where your audience actually spends their time. For example, platforms like TikTok are great for reaching a Gen Z population. According to Sprout’s 2026 Social Media Content Strategy Report , 72% of Gen Z social media users are on TikTok. So it makes sense for a startup like Scorability to maintain an active TikTok presence because the company connects athletes and high school teams with college coaches. And TikTok is where it can engage college-aged users. Source: TikTok Define your brand voice early Are you a brand that’s on top of the latest Gen Z slang? Do you speak to a professional audience that knows their industry language? Do you need a bold and empowering tone to inspire your audience? Or perhaps wit and sarcasm are baked into your brand identity. Think of how you want to speak to your audience even before you start creating content. Your brand voice will determine the type of language and tone to use in your marketing messages and social media posts. Use it consistently to stay on-brand as you craft captions and respond to customers on social media. Establish your content pillars What types of content are you going to post? Tie your ideas to 3-5 content pillars that align with your brand’s goals and target audience. For example, if your goal is to drive brand awareness and build community, you could do: Memes Humor-based skits Educational videos User-generated content As the 2026 Social Media Content Strategy Report shows, users expect brands to show up differently on each platform. So create platform-specific content pillars based on what resonates with users on each platform. For example, skits and humor videos will get more visibility on TikTok, while platforms like LinkedIn will need thought leadership and text posts. Decide your posting cadence per platform How often will you post on each platform? Some platforms require brands to post multiple times a day to maintain visibility. On other platforms, you risk overwhelming your audience if you post more than once a day. As you perfect your publishing cadence, make sure to time your posts strategically as well. Posts should go live at times that guarantee the most visibility and engagement in the first few minutes. Build a lightweight content calendar Once you have your content pillars and your posting cadence, organize everything in a content calendar. A social media calendar lets you visualize your content ideas and keep track of your posting schedules to maintain a consistent publishing strategy. It doesn’t have to be too complicated, either. Start with the essentials like: Publish date and time Format Caption/copy Format Creative asset Sprout’s Essentials plan comes with a visual content calendar where you can plan out your social media posts for the entire month across different platforms. Once you’ve outlined your publishing plan, you can start creating content in bulk to keep up with your publishing schedule. Use content batching to set aside time blocks to create all the posts you need for the rest of the week or month. title: Seabourn Quest Emerges from Dry Dock with Major Upgrades and Sustainability Enhancements
summary: When Seabourn Quest entered dry dock for the most extensive renovation in the ship’s history, the goal wasn’t simply to refresh guest spaces – it was also to rethink what happens to the materials being replaced. The result is a transformation that blends elevated luxury with sustainability efforts, giving thousands of onboard furnishings and materials a second life.
body_text: Snapshots Seabourn Quest Emerges from Dry Dock with Major Upgrades and Sustainability Enhancements Jul 14, 2026 Share When Seabourn Quest entered dry dock for the most extensive renovation in the ship’s history, the goal wasn’t simply to refresh guest spaces – it was also to rethink what happens to the materials being replaced. The result is a transformation that blends elevated luxury with sustainability efforts, giving thousands of onboard furnishings and materials a second life. More than 20,000 square meters of carpet removed during the renovation was diverted from landfill and is planned to be repurposed into new carpet padding for a future Seabourn renovation. Mattresses were deconstructed for recycling, lounge furnishings were donated to a local Italian nonprofit and updated suites now feature biodegradable Cradle to Cradle Dansk Wilton wool carpet to support a closed-loop lifecycle approach. The ship’s refreshed interiors now feature updated suites, dining venues, public spaces and wellness areas, designed to create an even warmer, more welcoming atmosphere. Since its upgrades, Seabourn Quest has resumed its Mediterranean sailings. Guests can experience the renewed ship while sailing itineraries throughout Croatia, Greece, Montenegro and Turkey. Share

title: Attio Email Integration: Log Deals From Your Inbox Automatically
summary: Stop manual CRM logging. Learn how to use the Attio email integration with Slashy to automate deal tracking, update pipeline stages, and see CRM context…
body_text: Founders connect Attio's native Gmail sync and assume the pipeline will manage itself. Once an email is sent, the deal record will update, the stage will shift, and the data will stay organized. That's not what happens. Attio's native integration is a data mirror, not an automation engine. It copies messages to contact records, but it does not understand the context of a deal or a specific fundraising round. By the end of this guide, you will have a workflow that eliminates manual logging entirely. You will move from a passive sync to an AI-native environment where your CRM lives inside your inbox. This process requires three things: an active Attio account, a Google Workspace inbox, and the Slashy desktop app. Stop switching tabs and start closing deals. Step 1: Understand What Attio's Native Gmail Sync Actually Does (and Doesn't) Attio is famous for its 'automatic' sync, but founders need to understand the technical boundaries. When you connect Gmail to Attio, the system creates a background process that copies every incoming and outgoing email into the 'Emails' tab of the corresponding person or company record. This is useful for record keeping and compliance. If a team member leaves, their history with a prospect stays intact. But this sync is entirely flat. Native sync does not understand the 'Deal' object. In Attio, deals are separate entities from people. If you are talking to a founder about a Series A investment, the native sync will attach that email to the founder's profile. It will not attach it to the 'Series A' deal record you created in your pipeline. You still have to click through the Attio UI to manually link the conversation to the specific deal. For a founder managing forty active conversations after a launch, that manual overhead adds up to hours every week. Native sync also gives you zero visibility inside your inbox. You cannot see if a person is already in your CRM while reading their email in Gmail. You cannot see their current pipeline stage or their LinkedIn profile without leaving your inbox. It is a one-way data dump from Gmail to Attio. To get real automation, you need a layer that sits on top of Gmail and talks directly to the Attio API in real time. Most early-stage operators get stuck here. They wait for Attio to fix the inbox, but the inbox is a separate product category. To bridge the gap, you need an intelligent client like Slashy. Step 2: Connect Your Gmail Account to Attio Before moving to advanced automation, establish the base connection. Log into your Attio workspace and navigate to the 'Settings' menu. Under the 'Integrations' tab, select 'Email and Calendar.' Here you will find the option to connect your Google Workspace account. Grant Attio permissions to read, send, and manage your mail. This is the foundation that allows Attio to start populating its internal database with your communication history. Once connected, configure your 'Privacy and Sharing' settings. Many founders skip this step. You can choose to share 'Metadata only' (subject lines and participants) or 'Full content.' For a small team, full content sharing is usually the right call. It lets everyone see the context of a deal without asking for forwarded threads. Attio uses TLS 1.2+ for data in transit, so the connection is secure from the start. After the sync completes, which can take several hours depending on inbox size, a new 'Emails' tab appears on every contact record. That confirms the data pipeline is active. Your history is now in Attio. You are still in the mirroring phase, though. The data is there, but it is not working for you. You are still the one doing the heavy lifting to keep the CRM updated as you reply throughout the day. To fix that, you have to look at the logging gaps the native integration leaves behind. Step 3: Identify the Logging Gaps That Require a Workaround The primary gap in the standard Attio email integration is the lack of deal context during the act of writing. When you are replying to a lead, you often need to know three things: the last note left by a teammate, the current deal value, and the next step in the pipeline. In a standard Gmail setup, you have to open a second browser tab, search for the contact in Attio, find the deal, and read the notes. That context switching is the silent killer of founder productivity. It turns a ten-second reply into a three-minute research project. Another major gap is pipeline progression. If you send a term sheet, the deal should move from 'Due Diligence' to 'Closing' automatically. Attio's native sync cannot do this because it cannot interpret the intent of your email. It just sees text. It doesn't know that 'Here is the signed agreement' means the deal is done. That requires a manual update in the Attio web app. For teams handling high volume, the result is a CRM that is always out of date. Stale data leads to missed follow-ups and double outreach, which looks unprofessional to high-value prospects. There is also the issue of multi-account management. Many founders use separate inboxes for different functions (a personal email and a generic 'founders@' or 'deals@' address). Managing these in a single CRM view is difficult when you are switching between browser profiles. You need a unified view that connects every inbox to your Attio database at the same time. Without it, you will inevitably miss logging a thread from your other account. To solve these gaps, use a client that treats the CRM as a first-class citizen, much like developers use an intelligent IDE for their code. Step 4: Connect Slashy as Your Email Client for Native Attio Logging Slashy is an AI-native email client that streamlines your workflow by acting as an intelligent layer for your inbox. It is built for founders who have outgrown the limitations of standard Gmail. Slashy is SOC 2 Type II certified and CASA Tier 2 certified, so it handles your deal data with enterprise-grade security. Your data is encrypted at rest using AES-256 and is never used to train AI models. To begin, download the Slashy Mac app or log in via the web. Connect your Gmail accounts. Slashy provides a unified inbox view, so you can see all your deal flow in one place without switching accounts. Slashy learns your writing style over time through its proprietary memory system. It looks at your sent messages and your Attio records to understand who you are talking to and what your relationship is. When a new email arrives from a prospect, Slashy doesn't just show you the text. It identifies the recipient and draws on per-recipient memory including preferences and context. You are no longer flying blind. You are operating from an intelligent inbox that understands the context of your conversations. Step 5: Use the Attio Sidebar to See Deal Context While You Reply One of the most immediate benefits of Slashy is the calendar sidebar. When you click on any email thread, a sidebar appears on the right side of your screen. This sidebar lives directly alongside the inbox so you can check availability and book meetings while replying. Slashy also uses its memory system to power its AI Draft Replies. When Slashy drafts a reply, it isn't just using the email thread for context. It looks at your previous threads and recipient context to draft replies in your voice. It produces a draft that sounds like you and includes relevant CRM data. You can then use the inline AI assistant to highlight a sentence and ask the AI to 'make this more professional' or 'add our booking link.' Every reply is informed by your actual availability, which prevents mistakes like asking for a meeting that is already on the calendar. Step 6: Set Up Auto-Logging Rules and Follow-Up Triggers The final step to zero manual logging is setting up automations. Inside Slashy, you can create automated workflows to handle your inbox busywork. For example, you can set a rule that automatically labels incoming emails so important messages rise to the top. Slashy's auto-labeling system pushes those messages to the top of your inbox so you never miss a time-sensitive contract or a closing question. One of the most useful features for founders is the follow-up reminder system. Deals go cold because a 'ping' gets forgotten after three days of silence. You can even set it to automatically draft a follow-up message in your voice, ready for you to review and send with one click. Pipeline velocity stays high without you manually tracking every ball in court. You can also use Slashy's scheduling features to insert your availability directly into an email. Slashy is connected to your calendar, so it knows when you are free. When a prospect clicks a time, it books the meeting and keeps your schedule synchronized. Your email, your calendar, and your CRM stay synchronized. You are no longer managing a CRM. You are doing your job, and the CRM is updating itself in the background. What to Do Next (and How to Troubleshoot Common Sync Issues) Start by auditing your current Attio setup. Confirm that your Gmail connection is active and that your privacy settings are on 'Full Content' to maximize visibility. If certain emails are not appearing in Attio, check your 'Excluded Domains' list in Attio settings. Founders often accidentally block internal domains or specific partners, which stops the sync from triggering. Also confirm you have not hit your API limit if you are running heavy third-party automations. If your CRM data is still scattered across tabs, it is time to switch your interface. Download the Slashy desktop app and spend one day working entirely from a native interface. Most founders report saving four to five hours a week just by cutting the context switch between Gmail and their CRM. Once the initial sync is complete, you can start using Slashy's AI search to find deal info by context (for example, 'who was the founder I talked to about seed extension?') rather than just keywords.
